title: PDEs Seminar – Swann Marx (CNRS, Nantes)
desc:
Title: Singular perturbation results for infinite-dimensional linear systems.

Abstract: Consider two coupled equations evolving on different time scales. A natural way to simplify the system is to set the time derivative in the fast equation to zero while retaining the slow equation. Can the resulting reduced model describes properly the stability of the full system? For ordinary differential equations, classical singular perturbation theory gives conditions under which stability of the reduced system and of the fast dynamics with the slow variables supposed fixed implies stability of the full system, provided the time scales are sufficiently far away to each other. In this talk, I will examine how far this principle extends to coupled systems involving partial differential equations.…

title: Junior Dynamics Seminar – Oscar Randles (Durham University)
desc:
Energy-constrained Brownian Motion

Speaker: Oscar Randles (Durham University)

Abstract : For reflected Brownian motion in an interval of length N, we consider the first time at which the length of time since the most recent visit to the boundary exceeds M; this random ‘lifetime’ comes from the interpretation in which the Brownian motion has a finite energy capacity M, uses energy at unit rate in the interior, and gets its energy replenished up to M on every visit to the boundary. We prove distributional asymptotics for the lifetime in three different regimes depending on the relative growth of N and M; these one-dimensional results parallel results in the random walk case by Wade and Grinfeld. We also present some initial results on the multidimensional version of the problem.

title: Engineering Topological Spin Textures in Three-Dimensional Magnetic Metamaterials
desc:
Dr. Naemi Leo, Loughborough University

Friday 27 th November 2026, B630, 11am

Abstract :

Confinement at the mesoscale gives rise to magnetic states and dynamical phenomena that have no counterparts in bulk materials. In this talk, I will discuss how three-dimensional magnetic metamaterials can be engineered to stabilize and control complex topological spin textures through geometry alone. Using magnetic nanohelices fabricated by focused electron beam induced deposition (FEBID), combined with x-ray magnetic circular dichroism microscopy and micromagnetic simulations, we demonstrate the controlled formation of metastable topological states, including Skyrmion tubes [1].

title: Junior Geometry Seminar – Natasha Diederen
desc:
Title: Topological change in mean curvature flow

Speaker: Natasha Diederen

Abstract: A hypersurface evolves by mean curvature flow if each point moves with velocity given by its mean curvature vector. This process is described by a nonlinear parabolic PDE and solutions form singularities in finite time. Mean curvature flow can be viewed as an extrinsic analogue to Ricci flow, and has similarly proved to be a useful tool in approaching various questions in geometry and topology. Addressing such questions requires an understanding of the formation and structure of singularities, as well as how the flow can be meaningfully extended past them. In this talk, we will explore, through a series of examples, what is known about the behaviour of mean curvature flow near singularities, and how…
